checks.a_analysis: The JSON output was reviewed for any repeated text blocks that do not exist in the source PDF. Instances where the same name or agency appears multiple times were verified against the source (e.g., Anna Hayworth represents multiple boards across different departments, and the contact information for several boards like the 911 Board and the ABC Commission lists two separate individuals). The linearization of the multi-column layout was checked at page and column boundaries to ensure no overlap or duplication occurred during chunk processing. No duplicated content was found.

The document title 'Rulemaking Coordinators' is correctly captured as the top-level section title (H1). The agency and board names, which serve as subheaders in the multi-column directory, have been flattened into paragraph elements. While this results in a flat hierarchy, it is an acceptable normalization for screen reader navigation in a directory format and does not involve skipped levels (e.g., H1 to H3) or incorrect nesting. The logical flow is maintained.

The source document contains no structured data tables. The multi-column layout consists of contact blocks, which have been correctly identified and converted into paragraphs in the JSON. Thus, no table corruption occurred.

The source document utilizes a three-column layout across 10 pages. The JSON conversion successfully linearizes this layout by processing columns top-to-bottom and left-to-right (linearizing Column 1, then Column 2, then Column 3 for each page). This preserves the logical flow of information for a directory. Verification at page transitions and column boundaries confirms that the order matches the visual flow intended by the source document.

The source document is a directory of contact information and does not contain traditional bulleted or numbered lists. The contact entries are structured as individual blocks, which are correctly represented as paragraphs in the JSON.

The JSON output correctly identifies and extracts email addresses and URLs from the source PDF. These are rendered as hyperlink objects within paragraph content with correct 'href' attributes (e.g., 'mailto:' links). No broken, missing, or fabricated links were identified during verification of major contact points.
